q: What is the virtual DOM / how does React decide what to update?
a: React renders components to a lightweight description, diffs it against the previous one (matching by type and key), and applies the minimal DOM changes. Keys are how list items are matched.
followUps: What happens with index keys on a reordered list?

q: Server Components vs Client Components in Next.js: when do you use each?
a: Default to Server Components for data fetching and static UI (zero client JS, secrets stay server-side). Use Client Components for state, effects, event handlers and browser APIs, pushing the boundary to small leaves.
followUps: What can't you pass from server to client component props?

q: A page refetches data in an endless loop. How do you debug?
a: Check the effect dependency array for values recreated each render (object/array literals, inline functions); confirm in Network; use stable references, useMemo, move constants out, or switch to TanStack Query with a stable key. Verify with a production build because Strict Mode double-invokes effects in dev.
followUps: How do you tell Strict Mode double calls from a real loop?

q: Users report seeing a different hour than the booked time. Investigate.
a: Check how the API sends times (offset?), how the UI formats (explicit timeZone?), the server vs browser zone, DST, and tests under another timezoneId. Fix with a single formatter using the business zone.

q: Design the booking page for 10x traffic and many concurrent users per slot.
a: Server-render the static shell, cache services, fetch availability client-side with short staleTime, never trust UI availability, rely on DB constraints/locks and 409 handling, add idempotency keys, rate limit, queue notifications, monitor conflict rates.
followUps: Where would you add caching and what would you not cache?

a: Controlled: value in React state. Uncontrolled: DOM keeps value, read via ref/form data. Libraries like React Hook Form use uncontrolled for performance.
